wire_correction_evidence.interpretation: Removing uniqueItems corrected a real current native-SDK incompatibility, but SDK acceptance did not predict routed provider acceptance.

next_design_constraints: Keep all completed semantic cases and their frozen request artifacts immutable.
Do not use the reserved agency-acquisition case to diagnose an operational schema failure.
Build a provider-free schema-reduction matrix before requesting any new call authority.
If calls are later authorized, use minimal non-semantic compatibility probes to isolate schema features before returning to valuable multi-turn cases.
Vary one schema dimension at a time and preserve exact request custody; do not add retries, fallback models, response healing, graph, or runtime behavior.
Do not weaken semantic representation merely to obtain a successful HTTP response without a separately reviewed product tradeoff.
nonclaims: The provider error did not identify a keyword, field, size, depth, enum, property, or array limit.
Native Google SDK acceptance is not provider acceptance.
No model output exists, so no stance interpretation, source fidelity, semantic accuracy, stability, product value, or trust was measured.
The repeated HTTP 400 responses do not show that stance objects are semantically wrong.
The local gates do not show that the provider wire is usable.
